extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and KIPO examiners dealing with patent term extension for delayed registration (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for filing, examining, and deciding applications to register patent term extensions due to delay in registration before the Korean Intellectual Property Office, including required contents, time limits, grounds, calculation of allowable extension, amendment and appeal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of application for registration of patent term extension (Article 92-3(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall state the following matters to the Commissioner: 1. The name and domicile of an applicant for registration of extension (if the applicant is a corporation, its name and the location of its business office); 2. The name and domicile of an agent, if any, or the location of his/her business office (if the agent is a patent firm or a limited-liability patent firm, its name, the location of its business office and the designated patent attorney’s name); 3. The number of a patent whose term is subject to extension; 4. The period of application for extension; 5. Grounds for extension prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (materials substantiating such grounds shall be attached thereto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may amend matters falling under paragraph (1) 4 and 5 before an examiner decides whether patent term extension shall be registered; after receiving a notice of grounds for rejection, amendments to those matters are allowed only during the period for submission of arguments following the notice. Attach evidential documents substantiating claimed grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to file application (Article 92-3(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for registration of patent term extension pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be filed within three months from the date of registration of a patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an application is filed before the date of registration or after three months have elapsed, an examiner shall give an opportunity of explanation under Article 11 of the Enforcement Rules and return the application. Formality section: examiner indicates intention to return, ground for return and period for explanation; documents may be returned if explanation is groundless or upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility and joint-owner requirement (Article 92-3(3) and 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent right is owned by joint owners, an application for registration of patent term extension shall be filed by all joint owners. An applicant of the application for registration of patent term extension due to a delay in registration is limited to a patent right holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the filer is not the patent right holder or co-owners fail to file, this constitutes a ground for rejection. Amendments that attempt to add co-owners after filing to cure this defect are generally not recognized (see notes on amendment and joint ownership).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attachments and written form (Enforcement Rules Article 54-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person intending to apply shall submit a written application of Annexed Form 30-2 with the following attached: 1. Ground for extension and a copy of the evidential document of the extension ground; 2. Where a representative conducts a proceeding, a power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure evidential documents are attached and power of attorney is provided when a representative files. The written form and attachments must conform to the Annexed Form requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated grounds for extension (Article 54-3 / Ordinance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for extension designated under Ordinance are: 1. Need to extend since the patent right was registered after four years from the filing date or three years from the date of request for examination, whichever later; 2. The period of request for extension and explanation that the period of delay attributable to an applicant is reduced from the period of request for extension under Article 92-2(2) and evidential document; 3. Other necessary items to prove the ground for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach evidential documents proving the ground(s). When stating the ground in the application, detail reductions of applicant-attributable delay (e.g., '123 days for submission of written argument') in the 'Period for Request for Registration of Extension' box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination and handling of defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application is in violation of formalities, the examiner shall: (1) for late filing (after three months) indicate intention to return and give period for explanation; (2) where violations concern representative designation, unpaid fees, or formalities specified in the Act/Decree, order amendment to the application; if irregularities are not addressed within the designated period, the examiner shall invalidate the patent-related proceeding in the name of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to notification of defects; request for return is possible; failure to cure ordered amendments leads to invalidation/termination of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of subject for examination when amendments are submitted (5.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject for examination is the application to register patent term extension and attached documents. Where amendment was made, the examiner shall determine whether to permit the amendment and specify the subject for examination. If legitimate, the examiner examines with amended content reflected; if not, the amendment is deemed never made and the pre-amendment application is examined. For multiple amendments, the finally-amended parts' combination defines the subject for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 'Determination Standard of Amended Content' for handling multiple/amended parts. Examiner may order amendment or issue preliminary notice of inadmissible amendment if amendment is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection grounds under Article 92-4
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall decide to reject the application where: 1. The length of extension requested exceeds a period of extension recognized pursuant to Article 92-2; 2. The applicant for registration of extension is not a patentee; 3. The application is filed in violation of Article 92-3(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner finds any of these, notify the ground for rejection and give opportunity to submit a written argument. The notice should state relevant provisions and grounds precisely and concisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of period allowed for requesting extension (detailed steps ①–⑤)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period allowed is the number of days (E) from the date of establishment of a patent right (D) based on the reference date (C)—the later of (A) four years from filing date of the patent application, or (B) three years after the date of request for examination—minus the period of delay attributable to an applicant (F) under Article 7-2(1) of the Enforcement Decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: ① Determine filing date (includes divisional, converted, certain international request dates, etc.); ② Determine later reference date between four years from filing and three years after request for examination; ③ Calculate total period of delay (days between reference date and establishment date after fee payment); ④ Sum periods of delay attributable to applicant (include Article 7-2(1) paragraphs; overlapping applicant delays should not reduce more than actual delay); ⑤ Subtract attributable delay from total delay to get allowable extension. If applicant's written request claims a longer period than calculated, examiner issues ground for rejection and allows written argument/amendment to correct items ①–⑤. An illustrated example and table are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from applicant-attributable delay (objective grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though a period falls under applicant-attributable categories, where there is any objectively-recognized ground that the delay in establishment of a patent right is not attributable to an applicant, such period shall be exempt from the period of delay attributable to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of exempted situations: delays happening before applicant requested examination, amendment order or notice of grounds for rejection made by mistake of KIPO or a patent court, delays caused by natural disasters, or other objectively-recognized grounds unrelated to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of ground for rejection and period for written argument
rubrics_metrics.description: When intending to reject, the examiner shall notify the ground(s) for rejection and give the applicant an opportunity to submit a written argument within a designated period. The notice must write relevant provisions or grounds precisely and concisely so the applicant clearly understands the ground for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard period for submission of a written argument is within two months; this period is extendable at the applicant's request up to four times, one month each. General information on notices is referred to PART V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of written arguments and amendments (5.4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice of ground for rejection, an applicant may submit a written argument or an amendment. A written argument can be submitted within the designated period; an amendment can be submitted until a certified copy of the decision to register is delivered, but after notification of grounds for rejection, amendments are only accepted within the written-argument period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner shall re-determine the presence of the ground for rejection considering submitted written arguments. Written arguments submitted late or before notice are accepted and referred for examination. Amendable parts under Article 92-3(4) include only: ① the period of request for extension and ② the ground for extension designated in Ordinance—changes to applicant or patent number are not allowed except for clerical corrections. If an inadmissible amendment is submitted, the examiner issues a preliminary notice of inadmissible amendment and gives opportunity to explain; if amendment remains unacceptable, examiner re-examines pre-amendment application and may replace notices with a written decision to reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on amendable parts (under Article 92-3(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendable parts in an application for registration of extension include only: ① the period of request for extension and ② the ground for extension designated in Ordinance of the Ministry of Knowledge Economy. Amendment of applicant name and patent number shall not be allowed except for correcting clerical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments changing the patent number would change the subject of registration and are therefore generally not recognized, except for correcting clerical errors (where filing date, patent number and patent date support clerical error claim). Amendments to add co-owners after filing to cure a joint-owner defect are not recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of recognition of amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an amendment is recognized to be legitimate, the amended application is recognized to have been filed in the first place; the examiner shall then conduct examination on the amended application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimate amendments retroactively alter the subject for examination and the filing status; ensure amendments are within permitted scope and timely submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision content and form for registration or rejection (5.4.5(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination on whether to extend the term shall be in writing. A decision to register extension or a decision to reject registration shall indicate: ① Application Number of Registration of Extension; ② Patent Number; ③ Period for Extension; ④ Content of Period of Delay; ⑤ Name and Address of Applicant; ⑥ Representative information if present; ⑦ Order and Ground for Decision; ⑧ Date of Decision. (A decision to reject shall not contain items ③ and ④.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must report intention to director/team head and sign and seal such decision. Details related to transmittal of certified copy follow provisions for decisions to grant/reject patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal and publication when extension is registered
rubrics_metrics.description: When registration for extension is determined, the Commissioner shall serve a certified copy of the decision. The Registration Division shall publish in the Patent Gazette: ① the name and address of the patent right holder, ② the patent number, ③ the date when the patent term extension is registered, ④ the period of extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow standard procedures for transmittal of certified copies and Gazette publication as with grant/reject decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal (trial) against decision to reject registration
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who received a decision to reject may submit a notice of appeal trial against the decision within thirty days from the date of transmittal of a certified copy of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Appeal Trial procedure and time limit (30 days) to challenge rejection decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation trial on patent right registered for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent right whose term is extended falls under any paragraph of Article 134-2 of the Patent Act, an interested party can request a trial to invalidate the patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation trials may be initiated post-registration of extension if statutory grounds under Article 134-2 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation on application for registration of extension
rubrics_metrics.description: An application to register patent term extension due to a delay in registration does not require a special authorization and can be carried out without special authorization. However, the scope of representation is somewhat ambiguous and refer to the chapter on 'Representation of Application for Registration of Extension of Patent Term for Approval, etc.' for details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a representative conducts the proceeding, submit a power of attorney. For scope and limits of representation (e.g., filing vs registration ambiguities), consult the indicated chapter (7.1.5).
